# Data Lakehouse Architecture – Pipeline & Governance

## Overview
This dataset describes a modern data lakehouse architecture following the medallion pattern (Bronze → Silver → Gold). It captures 10 data sources across 5 categories, 3 ingestion modes, 5 medallion-layer datasets per tier, 6 consumption endpoints, 15 governance controls, and transformation summaries per layer.

## Data Source

### architecture_nodes
Each record represents a component in the architecture. Fields: `node_id` (string, unique identifier), `label` (display name), `layer` (one of: source, ingestion, bronze, silver, gold, consumption), `category` (grouping within layer), `daily_volume_gb` (numeric or null for consumption nodes), `format` (data format or technology). 34 nodes total.

### architecture_edges
Directed edges between nodes. Fields: `edge_id` (string), `source` and `target` (node_id references), `volume_gb` (numeric or null), `mode` (streaming | batch | cdc | query), `latency` (descriptive string). 38 edges total.

### governance_controls
Governance policies applied per layer. Fields: `control_id`, `layer` (architecture layer or cross-layer), `control_type`, `tool`, `scope`, `enforcement` (automated | policy-based | manual | scheduled). 15 records.

### transformation_summary
Counts of transformation types per medallion layer. Fields: `layer`, `transformation_type`, `count` (integer), `complexity` (low | medium | high). 12 records across bronze, silver, and gold.

## Data Notes
- Volume figures are illustrative daily averages; actual volumes vary by day.
- Some bronze volumes exceed source totals due to log fan-out and metadata enrichment.
- Consumption-layer nodes have null volume as they represent query-based access.
- Governance controls tagged as "cross-layer" apply to the entire pipeline.

# Data Visualization Skill

Chart selection guidance, Python visualization code patterns, design principles, and accessibility considerations for creating effective data visualizations.

## Chart Selection Guide

### Choose by Data Relationship

| What You're Showing | Best Chart | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|
| **Trend over time** | Line chart | Area chart (if showing cumulative or composition) |
| **Comparison across categories** | Vertical bar chart | Horizontal bar (many categories), lollipop chart |
| **Ranking** | Horizontal bar chart | Dot plot, slope chart (comparing two periods) |
| **Part-to-whole composition** | Stacked bar chart | Treemap (hierarchical), waffle chart |
| **Composition over time** | Stacked area chart | 100% stacked bar (for proportion focus) |
| **Distribution** | Histogram | Box plot (comparing groups), violin plot, strip plot |
| **Correlation (2 variables)** | Scatter plot | Bubble chart (add 3rd variable as size) |
| **Correlation (many variables)** | Heatmap (correlation matrix) | Pair plot |
| **Geographic patterns** | Choropleth map | Bubble map, hex map |
| **Flow / process** | Sankey diagram | Funnel chart (sequential stages) |
| **Relationship network** | Network graph | Chord diagram |
| **Performance vs. target** | Bullet chart | Gauge (single KPI only) |
| **Multiple KPIs at once** | Small multiples | Dashboard with separate charts |

### When NOT to Use Certain Charts

- **Pie charts**: Avoid unless <6 categories and exact proportions matter less than rough comparison. Humans are bad at comparing angles. Use bar charts instead.
- **3D charts**: Never. They distort perception and add no information.
- **Dual-axis charts**: Use cautiously. They can mislead by implying correlation. Clearly label both axes if used.
- **Stacked bar (many categories)**: Hard to compare middle segments. Use small multiples or grouped bars instead.
- **Donut charts**: Slightly better than pie charts but same fundamental issues. Use for single KPI display at most.

## Python Visualization Code Patterns

### Setup and Style

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Professional style setup
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
plt.rcParams.update({
    'figure.figsize': (10, 6),
    'figure.dpi': 150,
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 14,
    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    'axes.labelsize': 11,
    'xtick.labelsize': 10,
    'ytick.labelsize': 10,
    'legend.fontsize': 10,
    'figure.titlesize': 16,
})

# Colorblind-friendly palettes
PALETTE_CATEGORICAL = ['#4C72B0', '#DD8452', '#55A868', '#C44E52', '#8172B3', '#937860']
PALETTE_SEQUENTIAL = 'YlOrRd'
PALETTE_DIVERGING = 'RdBu_r'
```

### Line Chart (Time Series)

```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

for label, group in df.groupby('category'):
    ax.plot(group['date'], group['value'], label=label, linewidth=2)

ax.set_title('Metric Trend by Category', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Date')
ax.set_ylabel('Value')
ax.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True)
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# Format dates on x-axis
fig.autofmt_xdate()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('trend_chart.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
```

### Bar Chart (Comparison)

```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

# Sort by value for easy reading
df_sorted = df.sort_values('metric', ascending=True)

bars = ax.barh(df_sorted['category'], df_sorted['metric'], color=PALETTE_CATEGORICAL[0])

# Add value labels
for bar in bars:
    width = bar.get_width()
    ax.text(width + 0.5, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2,
            f'{width:,.0f}', ha='left', va='center', fontsize=10)

ax.set_title('Metric by Category (Ranked)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Metric Value')
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('bar_chart.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
```

### Histogram (Distribution)

```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

ax.hist(df['value'], bins=30, color=PALETTE_CATEGORICAL[0], edgecolor='white', alpha=0.8)

# Add mean and median lines
mean_val = df['value'].mean()
median_val = df['value'].median()
ax.axvline(mean_val, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, label=f'Mean: {mean_val:,.1f}')
ax.axvline(median_val, color='green', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, label=f'Median: {median_val:,.1f}')

ax.set_title('Distribution of Values', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Value')
ax.set_ylabel('Frequency')
```

## Design Principles

### Color

- **Use color purposefully**: Color should encode data, not decorate
- **Highlight the story**: Use a bright accent color for the key insight; grey everything else
- **Sequential data**: Use a single-hue gradient (light to dark) for ordered values
- **Diverging data**: Use a two-hue gradient with neutral midpoint for data with a meaningful center
- **Categorical data**: Use distinct hues, maximum 6-8 before it gets confusing
- **Avoid red/green only**: 8% of men are red-green colorblind. Use blue/orange as primary pair

### Typography

- **Title states the insight**: "Revenue grew 23% YoY" beats "Revenue by Month"
- **Subtitle adds context**: Date range, filters applied, data source
- **Axis labels are readable**: Never rotated 90 degrees if avoidable. Shorten or wrap instead
- **Data labels add precision**: Use on key points, not every single bar
- **Annotation highlights**: Call out specific points with text annotations

### Layout

- **Reduce chart junk**: Remove gridlines, borders, backgrounds that don't carry information
- **Sort meaningfully**: Categories sorted by value (not alphabetically) unless there's a natural order (months, stages)
- **Appropriate aspect ratio**: Time series wider than tall (3:1 to 2:1); comparisons can be squarer
- **White space is good**: Don't cram charts together. Give each visualization room to breathe

### Accuracy

- **Bar charts start at zero**: Always. A bar from 95 to 100 exaggerates a 5% difference
- **Line charts can have non-zero baselines**: When the range of variation is meaningful
- **Consistent scales across panels**: When comparing multiple charts, use the same axis range
- **Show uncertainty**: Error bars, confidence intervals, or ranges when data is uncertain
- **Label your axes**: Never make the reader guess what the numbers mean

## Accessibility Considerations

### Color Blindness

- Never rely on color alone to distinguish data series
- Add pattern fills, different line styles (solid, dashed, dotted), or direct labels
- Test with a colorblind simulator (e.g., Coblis, Sim Daltonism)
- Use the colorblind-friendly palette: `sns.color_palette("colorblind")`

### Screen Readers

- Include alt text describing the chart's key finding
- Provide a data table alternative alongside the visualization
- Use semantic titles and labels

### General Accessibility

- Sufficient contrast between data elements and background
- Text size minimum 10pt for labels, 12pt for titles
- Avoid conveying information only through spatial position (add labels)
- Consider printing: does the chart work in black and white?

### Accessibility Checklist

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch
import numpy as np
import json

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

nodes = data['architecture_nodes']['data']
edges = data['architecture_edges']['data']
transformations = data['transformation_summary']['data']
governance = data['governance_controls']['data']

# Define layer colors (business theme)
LAYER_COLORS = {
    'source': '#2E86AB',
    'ingestion': '#A23B72',
    'bronze': '#F18F01',
    'silver': '#C73E1D',
    'gold': '#3B1F2B',
    'consumption': '#44AF69'
}

# Group nodes by layer
layers = ['source', 'ingestion', 'bronze', 'silver', 'gold', 'consumption']
layer_nodes = {layer: [] for layer in layers}
for node in nodes:
    layer_nodes[node['layer']].append(node)

# Calculate totals for scaling
total_source = sum(node['daily_volume_gb'] for node in layer_nodes['source'])
total_bronze = sum(node['daily_volume_gb'] for node in layer_nodes['bronze'])
total_silver = sum(node['daily_volume_gb'] for node in layer_nodes['silver'])
total_gold = sum(node['daily_volume_gb'] for node in layer_nodes['gold'])

# Transformation counts by layer
trans_counts = {}
for t in transformations:
    layer = t['layer']
    if layer not in trans_counts:
        trans_counts[layer] = {'total': 0, 'high': 0, 'medium': 0}
    trans_counts[layer]['total'] += t['count']
    if t['complexity'] == 'high':
        trans_counts[layer]['high'] += t['count']
    elif t['complexity'] == 'medium':
        trans_counts[layer]['medium'] += t['count']

cross_layer_gov = sum(1 for g in governance if g['layer'] == 'cross-layer')

# Create figure
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(20, 12))
ax.set_xlim(0, 100)
ax.set_ylim(0, 80)
ax.axis('off')

# Layer positions (x centers)
LAYOUT_X = {
    'source': 10,
    'ingestion': 26,
    'bronze': 42,
    'silver': 58,
    'gold': 74,
    'consumption': 90
}

# Draw horizontal band for each layer
def draw_layer_band(ax, layer_name, layer_color, nodes, y_base=40, height=25):
    """Draw a horizontal band showing nodes in a layer with flows."""
    x = LAYOUT_X[layer_name]
    band_h = 20

    # Draw layer background
    rect = FancyBboxPatch((x - 8, y_base - band_h/2), 16, band_h,
                          boxstyle="round,pad=0.02,rounding_size=1.5",
                          facecolor=layer_color, edgecolor='white',
                          linewidth=3, alpha=0.2)
    ax.add_patch(rect)

    # Calculate vertical positions for nodes
    node_count = len(nodes)
    spacing = band_h / (node_count + 1)

    node_positions = []
    for i, node in enumerate(nodes):
        y_pos = y_base + band_h/2 - spacing * (i + 1)
        vol = node['daily_volume_gb'] if node['daily_volume_gb'] is not None else 0

        # Draw node box
        box_w = 10
        box_h = 4 if vol > 0 else 2.5
        box = FancyBboxPatch((x - box_w/2, y_pos - box_h/2), box_w, box_h,
                            boxstyle="round,pad=0.02,rounding_size=0.8",
                            facecolor=layer_color, edgecolor='white',
                            linewidth=2, alpha=0.9)
        ax.add_patch(box)

        # Node label
        label = node['label']
        if len(label) > 12:
            label = label[:10] + '...'
        ax.text(x, y_pos, label, ha='center', va='center',
                fontsize=7, color='white', fontweight='bold')

        # Volume label
        vol_text = f"{vol:,}" if vol > 0 else "Query"
        ax.text(x - box_w/2 - 0.5, y_pos, vol_text,
                ha='right', va='center', fontsize=6, color=layer_color)

        node_positions.append({'node_id': node['node_id'], 'y': y_pos, 'x': x})
        edge_y = y_pos

    return node_positions

# Draw each layer
node_positions = {}
for layer in layers:
    node_positions[layer] = draw_layer_band(ax, layer, LAYER_COLORS[layer], layer_nodes[layer])

# Layer labels at top
layer_labels = {
    'source': 'SOURCE\n10 Data Sources\n1,560 GB/day',
    'ingestion': 'INGESTION\n3 Engines\n1,560 GB/day',
    'bronze': 'BRONZE\n5 Raw Tables\n1,560 GB/day',
    'silver': 'SILVER\n5 Curated Sets\n445 GB/day',
    'gold': 'GOLD\n5 Business Sets\n32 GB/day',
    'consumption': 'CONSUMPTION\n6 Endpoints\nQuery-based'
}

for layer, x in LAYOUT_X.items():
    ax.text(x, 58, layer_labels[layer], ha='center', va='top',
            fontsize=9, fontweight='bold', color=LAYER_COLORS[layer],
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor=LAYER_COLORS[layer], alpha=0.15))

# Draw flow connections between layers
def draw_flows(ax, from_layer, to_layer, edges, alpha=0.3):
    """Draw flows between layers based on edges."""
    x1 = LAYOUT_X[from_layer] + 5
    x2 = LAYOUT_X[to_layer] - 5

    from_positions = {n['node_id']: n for n in node_positions[from_layer]}
    to_positions = {n['node_id']: n for n in node_positions[to_layer]}

    for edge in edges:
        if edge['source'] in from_positions and edge['target'] in to_positions:
            from_y = from_positions[edge['source']]['y']
            to_y = to_positions[edge['target']]['y']
            vol = edge['volume_gb'] or 10
            width = min(vol / 150, 2.5)

            # Color by mode
            mode_colors = {'streaming': '#4C72B0', 'batch': '#DD8452', 'cdc': '#55A868', 'query': '#C44E52'}
            color = mode_colors.get(edge['mode'], '#AAAAAA')

            ax.annotate('', xy=(x2, to_y), xytext=(x1, from_y),
                       arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=color, alpha=alpha,
                                     connectionstyle='arc3,rad=0.1', lw=max(0.5, width)))

# Get edges between consecutive layers
source_edges = [e for e in edges if 'src_' in e['source'] and 'ing_' in e['target']]
ingestion_edges = [e for e in edges if 'ing_' in e['source'] and 'brz_' in e['target']]
bronze_edges = [e for e in edges if 'brz_' in e['source'] and 'slv_' in e['target']]
silver_edges = [e for e in edges if 'slv_' in e['source'] and 'gld_' in e['target']]
gold_edges = [e for e in edges if 'gld_' in e['source'] and 'con_' in e['target']]

draw_flows(ax, 'source', 'ingestion', source_edges, alpha=0.25)
draw_flows(ax, 'ingestion', 'bronze', ingestion_edges, alpha=0.25)
draw_flows(ax, 'bronze', 'silver', bronze_edges, alpha=0.25)
draw_flows(ax, 'silver', 'gold', silver_edges, alpha=0.25)
draw_flows(ax, 'gold', 'consumption', gold_edges, alpha=0.25)

# Add title
ax.text(50, 76, 'Data Lakehouse Architecture: End-to-End Pipeline Data Flow',
        ha='center', va='top', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', color='#1a1a1a')
ax.text(50, 73, 'Medallion Pattern (Bronze → Silver → Gold) | Arrows show data flow volume',
        ha='center', va='top', fontsize=10, color='#666666')

# Add legend for flow modes
legend_elements = [
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor='#4C72B0', label='Streaming'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor='#DD8452', label='Batch'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor='#55A868', label='CDC'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor='#C44E52', label='Query')
]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='lower right', title='Flow Modes',
         fontsize=9, title_fontsize=10, framealpha=0.9)

# Add transformation summary at bottom
trans_text = "Transformations: "
for layer in ['bronze', 'silver', 'gold']:
    if layer in trans_counts:
        tc = trans_counts[layer]
        trans_text += f"{layer.upper()}: {tc['total']} (H:{tc['high']}/M:{tc['medium']})  "

ax.text(50, 4, trans_text, ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9, color='#444444',
        style='italic')

# Governance note
gov_text = f"Governance: {len(governance)} controls across layers | {cross_layer_gov} cross-cutting (Lineage, Classification, Compliance)"
ax.text(50, 1.5, gov_text, ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9, color='#444444',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='#f5f5f5', alpha=0.8))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
print("Chart saved to /app/output/result.png")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch
import numpy as np
import json

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

nodes = data['architecture_nodes']['data']
edges = data['architecture_edges']['data']
transformations = data['transformation_summary']['data']
governance = data['governance_controls']['data']

# Define layer colors (business theme)
LAYER_COLORS = {
    'source': '#2E86AB',
    'ingestion': '#A23B72',
    'bronze': '#F18F01',
    'silver': '#C73E1D',
    'gold': '#3B1F2B',
    'consumption': '#44AF69'
}

# Group nodes by layer
layers = ['source', 'ingestion', 'bronze', 'silver', 'gold', 'consumption']
layer_nodes = {layer: [] for layer in layers}
for node in nodes:
    layer_nodes[node['layer']].append(node)

# Calculate totals for scaling
total_source = sum(node['daily_volume_gb'] for node in layer_nodes['source'])
total_bronze = sum(node['daily_volume_gb'] for node in layer_nodes['bronze'])
total_silver = sum(node['daily_volume_gb'] for node in layer_nodes['silver'])
total_gold = sum(node['daily_volume_gb'] for node in layer_nodes['gold'])

# Transformation counts by layer
trans_counts = {}
for t in transformations:
    layer = t['layer']
    if layer not in trans_counts:
        trans_counts[layer] = {'total': 0, 'high': 0, 'medium': 0}
    trans_counts[layer]['total'] += t['count']
    if t['complexity'] == 'high':
        trans_counts[layer]['high'] += t['count']
    elif t['complexity'] == 'medium':
        trans_counts[layer]['medium'] += t['count']

cross_layer_gov = sum(1 for g in governance if g['layer'] == 'cross-layer')

# Create figure
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(20, 12))
ax.set_xlim(0, 100)
ax.set_ylim(0, 80)
ax.axis('off')

# Layer positions (x centers)
LAYOUT_X = {
    'source': 10,
    'ingestion': 26,
    'bronze': 42,
    'silver': 58,
    'gold': 74,
    'consumption': 90
}

# Draw horizontal band for each layer
def draw_layer_band(ax, layer_name, layer_color, nodes, y_base=40, height=25):
    """Draw a horizontal band showing nodes in a layer with flows."""
    x = LAYOUT_X[layer_name]
    band_h = 20

    # Draw layer background
    rect = FancyBboxPatch((x - 8, y_base - band_h/2), 16, band_h,
                          boxstyle="round,pad=0.02,rounding_size=1.5",
                          facecolor=layer_color, edgecolor='white',
                          linewidth=3, alpha=0.2)
    ax.add_patch(rect)

    # Calculate vertical positions for nodes
    node_count = len(nodes)
    spacing = band_h / (node_count + 1)

    node_positions = []
    for i, node in enumerate(nodes):
        y_pos = y_base + band_h/2 - spacing * (i + 1)
        vol = node['daily_volume_gb'] if node['daily_volume_gb'] is not None else 0

        # Draw node box
        box_w = 10
        box_h = 4 if vol > 0 else 2.5
        box = FancyBboxPatch((x - box_w/2, y_pos - box_h/2), box_w, box_h,
                            boxstyle="round,pad=0.02,rounding_size=0.8",
                            facecolor=layer_color, edgecolor='white',
                            linewidth=2, alpha=0.9)
        ax.add_patch(box)

        # Node label
        label = node['label']
        if len(label) > 12:
            label = label[:10] + '...'
        ax.text(x, y_pos, label, ha='center', va='center',
                fontsize=7, color='white', fontweight='bold')

        # Volume label
        vol_text = f"{vol:,}" if vol > 0 else "Query"
        ax.text(x - box_w/2 - 0.5, y_pos, vol_text,
                ha='right', va='center', fontsize=6, color=layer_color)

        node_positions.append({'node_id': node['node_id'], 'y': y_pos, 'x': x})
        edge_y = y_pos

    return node_positions

# Draw each layer
node_positions = {}
for layer in layers:
    node_positions[layer] = draw_layer_band(ax, layer, LAYER_COLORS[layer], layer_nodes[layer])

# Layer labels at top
layer_labels = {
    'source': 'SOURCE\n10 Data Sources\n1,560 GB/day',
    'ingestion': 'INGESTION\n3 Engines\n1,560 GB/day',
    'bronze': 'BRONZE\n5 Raw Tables\n1,560 GB/day',
    'silver': 'SILVER\n5 Curated Sets\n445 GB/day',
    'gold': 'GOLD\n5 Business Sets\n32 GB/day',
    'consumption': 'CONSUMPTION\n6 Endpoints\nQuery-based'
}

for layer, x in LAYOUT_X.items():
    ax.text(x, 58, layer_labels[layer], ha='center', va='top',
            fontsize=9, fontweight='bold', color=LAYER_COLORS[layer],
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor=LAYER_COLORS[layer], alpha=0.15))

# Draw flow connections between layers
def draw_flows(ax, from_layer, to_layer, edges, alpha=0.3):
    """Draw flows between layers based on edges."""
    x1 = LAYOUT_X[from_layer] + 5
    x2 = LAYOUT_X[to_layer] - 5

    from_positions = {n['node_id']: n for n in node_positions[from_layer]}
    to_positions = {n['node_id']: n for n in node_positions[to_layer]}

    for edge in edges:
        if edge['source'] in from_positions and edge['target'] in to_positions:
            from_y = from_positions[edge['source']]['y']
            to_y = to_positions[edge['target']]['y']
            vol = edge['volume_gb'] or 10
            width = min(vol / 150, 2.5)

            # Color by mode
            mode_colors = {'streaming': '#4C72B0', 'batch': '#DD8452', 'cdc': '#55A868', 'query': '#C44E52'}
            color = mode_colors.get(edge['mode'], '#AAAAAA')

            ax.annotate('', xy=(x2, to_y), xytext=(x1, from_y),
                       arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=color, alpha=alpha,
                                     connectionstyle='arc3,rad=0.1', lw=max(0.5, width)))

# Get edges between consecutive layers
source_edges = [e for e in edges if 'src_' in e['source'] and 'ing_' in e['target']]
ingestion_edges = [e for e in edges if 'ing_' in e['source'] and 'brz_' in e['target']]
bronze_edges = [e for e in edges if 'brz_' in e['source'] and 'slv_' in e['target']]
silver_edges = [e for e in edges if 'slv_' in e['source'] and 'gld_' in e['target']]
gold_edges = [e for e in edges if 'gld_' in e['source'] and 'con_' in e['target']]

draw_flows(ax, 'source', 'ingestion', source_edges, alpha=0.25)
draw_flows(ax, 'ingestion', 'bronze', ingestion_edges, alpha=0.25)
draw_flows(ax, 'bronze', 'silver', bronze_edges, alpha=0.25)
draw_flows(ax, 'silver', 'gold', silver_edges, alpha=0.25)
draw_flows(ax, 'gold', 'consumption', gold_edges, alpha=0.25)

# Add title
ax.text(50, 76, 'Data Lakehouse Architecture: End-to-End Pipeline Data Flow',
        ha='center', va='top', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', color='#1a1a1a')
ax.text(50, 73, 'Medallion Pattern (Bronze → Silver → Gold) | Arrows show data flow volume',
        ha='center', va='top', fontsize=10, color='#666666')

# Add legend for flow modes
legend_elements = [
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor='#4C72B0', label='Streaming'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor='#DD8452', label='Batch'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor='#55A868', label='CDC'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor='#C44E52', label='Query')
]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='lower right', title='Flow Modes',
         fontsize=9, title_fontsize=10, framealpha=0.9)

# Add transformation summary at bottom
trans_text = "Transformations: "
for layer in ['bronze', 'silver', 'gold']:
    if layer in trans_counts:
        tc = trans_counts[layer]
        trans_text += f"{layer.upper()}: {tc['total']} (H:{tc['high']}/M:{tc['medium']})  "

ax.text(50, 4, trans_text, ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9, color='#444444',
        style='italic')

# Governance note
gov_text = f"Governance: {len(governance)} controls across layers | {cross_layer_gov} cross-cutting (Lineage, Classification, Compliance)"
ax.text(50, 1.5, gov_text, ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9, color='#444444',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='#f5f5f5', alpha=0.8))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
print("Chart saved to /app/output/result.png")
